name: Silverstone 2026 qualifying
what: Measured track model: fused centreline, corner geometry and the real field's driving statistics from 22 qualifying laps
sources: Telemetry: OpenF1 (api.openf1.org/v1) via concept/data/telemetry (see its README for licence and method)
Corner markers: MultiViewer circuit API (api.multiviewer.app), as used by FastF1 get_circuit_info()
Centreline: OpenStreetMap (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0, via js/data/silverstone.js
Official length, sector splits and straight-mode zones: concept/data/silverstone-2026-weekend.json (FIA documents cited there)

units.distance: m along the model centreline from the timing line
units.stats: {mean, std (sample, n-1), min, max, n} across drivers

geometry.frame: F1 timing frame (OpenF1 x/y / 10, metres), assumed right-handed

elevation.note: relative height (m) from the elevation profile in js/data/silverstone.js, mapped by lap fraction; that file does not document its elevation source, so treat as indicative

straight_mode_zones.straight: T14 to T15 (the straight with the speed trap, 140m before T15)
